newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates stable in boosted supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates stable in boosted supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were stable to slightly higher in moderate morning trade characterised by boosted supply, despite current monthly pension payments.
"We saw increase in supply for both call-money and term loans," dealer Jasenka Blagaic said.
She said fresh borrowings accounted for most of 31 million kuna ($5.2 million) of morning settlemsts. Of this, 18 million were call money deals at a stedy 10.5 percent rate.
Most term money was one-month borrowings at 15 percent, while a single 1.1 million two-month loan was struck at 17 percent.
Supply overshot offers by 20 million. One bank sought a two million loan but could not agree on terms.
Tuesday's overnight trade was meagre at 110 million kuna as two banks needed funds for their mandatory reserves.
-- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.015 Croatian Kuna)
